name: feature-scroll-section
purpose: The walkthrough band of a product page: a large section title over one screen per feature. From the large breakpoint up the features scroll through a sticky stack — the copy advances while the feature's live scene or illustration stays pinned in a framed, textured stage with one small action under each step (a step may pin a one-file code sample instead, for a code-led walkthrough); below it the same features are a three-column grid of media tiles. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'feature-scroll-section', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `registration-frame`, `card-grid`, `media-tile`, `illustration`, `code-block`, `sticky-stack`, `texture`, `button` and the webkit scene assets (a `ConsoleMockup` console fragment, most often).
useWhen: Use FeatureScrollSection for the product-page walkthrough, one pinned screen (scene or code) per feature.
To walk through four to six capabilities of one product, each with a picture of its own.
To walk through capabilities each shown by the file you would write: give each item a `code` sample. It is the code slot of a marketing page: media bands show no code.
avoidWhen: For three reasons with no scroll story → use `feature-tiles-section`.
In a hand-built SFC that needs its own media slot → use `sticky-stack` directly.
related: `sticky-stack` — the scroll engine the large layout runs on.
`media-tile` — the cell the small layout renders each feature with.
bestPractices: Four to six items; the stack needs enough steps to earn the scroll.

Give every item a `scene`, a `code` sample or an `illustration`; it is the pinned picture on large screens and the tile media on small ones. On a product page prefer a `scene` naming a `ConsoleMockup` (`{ component: 'ConsoleMockup', props: { name } }`): it shows the console itself.
Keep `action` to a short label such as "Docs" — it sits under the step copy at the small size.

props.name: anchor
props.doc: In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it.

props.name: title
props.doc: Headline of the band, rendered by the large section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty.

props.name: items
props.doc: The features, in order; each is `{ title, description, scene?, code?, illustration?, action? }` where `scene` is `{ component, props? }` naming a webkit scene asset (drawn live in the stack, still in the grid), `code` is a one-file sample `{ fileName, code, language?, fileIcon?, copyAriaLabel? }` drawn when no scene is set, `illustration` is a registry name drawn when neither is set, and `action` is `{ label, href, trailing?, target?, variant? }` rendered as a small button under the step, secondary unless `variant` says otherwise.
